requirements.statement: Every task card shows exactly one stage, readable without opening the task. The stages are: not started; being worked on; waiting for an answer or blocked; waiting for review; under review; sent back; approved, waiting to land; checking; landing; on main; landing held; did not land; closed without landing.

requirements.rationale: The status 'approved' says a reviewer agreed. It does not say the work reached main, and those are the moments the operator needs to tell apart.
requirements.statement: A card's stage reflects what is actually happening, not only the task's status column. A task is 'being worked on' only while a run bound to that task is running. It is 'on main' only once its work has landed on the main branch. An approved task whose work has not landed is never shown as on main.
A card at 'on main' shows the short commit id its work landed at. A card at 'landing held' shows what it waits on. A card at 'did not land' shows why, in one line.

requirements.rationale: A task stuck for days must look different from one that moved a minute ago; nothing on the card shows that today.
requirements.statement: Every card shows how long its task has been at its current stage, measured from when it entered that stage, in a compact form ('14 min', '2 days'). The duration advances while the board is open, at least once a minute.

When a task is waiting (for an answer, blocked, held, or not started because of prerequisites), its card names what it waits on in one line. That is one of: the agent whose question is open, the id of each unfinished task it depends on, or the name of the failing check or held item. A task not waiting shows no such line.
On the board, a task that is on main is visually distinct from an approved task not yet on main. The operator can tell them apart without reading the stage text.
Without opening any task, the board shows how many tasks are approved but not yet on main, and lets the operator see which ones. The same applies to tasks being worked on.

A card's stage, its waits-on line and the counts from not-yet-on-main change within 5 seconds of the underlying change (a run ending, a landing finishing, a prerequisite completing), without a page reload.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-11: one clear name, the holder at completion, rather than every agent that ran on the task.
requirements.statement: When a task moves to completed, it records as its builder the agent holding it at that moment. That name stays unchanged when the task is handed to a reviewer or tester, inside or outside a flow. If the task is sent back and completed again, the builder becomes whoever holds it at that later completion.
From 'waiting for review' onward, a card and the task drawer show the builder and the current reviewer as two separately labelled names. A task never reviewed shows only its builder.
The spec filter lists specs ordered by the most recent activity on any of their tasks (created or moved), newest first. 'All', 'Building' and 'No spec' stay at the top.
Each spec in the filter shows its short tag, how long ago its last task activity was ('2 h', '3 days'), and how many of its tasks are not finished.
Typing in the filter matches any spec whose short tag or title contains the typed text, case-insensitively, keeping the recency order.

requirements.rationale: A written tag reads well; the derived fallback means existing specs, and authors who skip the field, still get one (operator, 2026-11-12).
requirements.statement: Every spec has a short tag of at most 24 characters, unique within the project. The spec's author may write it when submitting the document; a spec with no written tag gets one derived from its title. Every card of a task belonging to a spec shows that tag.
By default the board shows no finished task. A task is finished when it is on main or closed without landing. The board states how many finished tasks it is hiding.
A 'show finished' switch on the board brings finished tasks back into view, marked as finished. The choice is remembered per project.

requirements.rationale: Looking up one old task should not require switching the whole board to show everything.
requirements.statement: The board's search also finds finished tasks while 'show finished' is off, showing them marked as finished.

A card shows only: its title; its stage as a glyph and a word; time at stage; the waits-on line when waiting; builder and reviewer; its spec's short tag; a failing-checks marker; and priority only when critical.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-12: what a card is stuck on is actionable, how long it has been stuck is not.
requirements.statement: Apart from its title, no card shows more than two lines of text at the board's default width. When the waits-on line and time at stage do not both fit, waits-on is kept and time at stage gives way; when names are long, the builder's name is cut before the reviewer's.
Description, branch, commits, requirements and acceptance criteria appear in the opened task and never on the card.
A task whose latest checks failed shows, before review, a marker on its card naming how many checks failed. Opening the task lists them in its Work view.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-12: answered questions record decisions, which is what is looked for later.
requirements.statement: The Story keeps every link it has today (traces, conversations) and shows each entry as a glyph, a label of at most six words, the actor and the time. Runs of four or more consecutive routine entries fold into one entry that opens. These are never folded: created, finished building, approved, sent back, landed or did not land, closed, any failure, anything waiting on the operator, and questions the operator answered. Any entry can be expanded to its full text.

The opened task has a Work view listing the requirements it serves, each with its evidence state read from the document's coverage, the requirement's acceptance criteria, and the latest checks with their outcome. An Earlier runs control shows the checks of previous runs.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-12: fewer changes; dropping today's controls was rejected.
requirements.statement: The opened task's Details view shows description, waits-on and needed-by tasks, notes, facts, history and escalation, and keeps every control today's Details offers. Facts never repeat their label in their value (no 'Built by: built by Developer').
A card changing stage animates the change, finishing within 300 ms. With reduced motion requested by the system, no animation plays and the change still shows.
Colours, type and glyphs come from AgentWeave's identity kit, in both light and dark themes.
No stage or marker is conveyed by colour alone. All card and story text meets WCAG AA contrast in both themes.
